newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Competition for world's largest flower auction.
newsitem.headline: Competition for world's largest flower auction.

text.p: The long term economic success of the worlds largest flower auction, Bloemenveiling Aalsmeer in the Netherlands, depends to a large degree on its response to new competition, its managing director told Reuters.

In an interview, Andre Mulder, managing director, of the big Dutch flower auction said it increasingly faces tough competition from non-Dutch growers which in recent years have made in-roads into the European market with high quality flowers and plants.
"We are telling our growers and buyers, lets be clear: the international flower market is growing fast, especially in Africa."
The auction, which is run by a large co-operative assocation of Dutch growers, has to adapt to the new market conditions, said Mulder.
"We must respond to this trend, otherwise we will lose our dominant position. However, we are saying to our membership, take care of your sales in this more difficult market."

Mulder said Germany is likely to remain the most important market for the auction, accounting for 40 percent of its turnover. Last year, the auction had a turnover of 2.4 billion Guilders, for a net profit of 13.5 million Guilders.
But he said there are signs of change. "This year, Russia all of sudden is our third most important country. It might be possible in the long run that it will increase in importance."

Other markets are, however, opening up. We had an interesting turnover in the U.S. up until 1986 or 1987 when there was a dramatic change in the exchange rate between the dollar and guilder. If you compare our flowers with those of Mexico, Columbia and South America, we are more expensive," he added.

"However, we think there is the possibility to do more business and I am sure our exporters will make continuing efforts in this market in the coming years. The same can be said of the Baltic Countries and Asia, other markets where we see growth in the future."
